Commentary.Commentary: The Proteas pacers bowled well initially. They made most of the swing but credit to the Indian openers who didn't take much risk at that time but once the ball got soft, they banged it in all corners of the ground. South Africa Women bowled below their standards. Even their fielding was not up to the mark. They dropped a couple of chances and easy ones at crucial times and just allowed India to enjoy their merry way. Right then! A must-win game and South Africa Women have a big task ahead. They succumbed in the last match but can't afford it again or else they would lose the series. Stay tuned for the chase.

India started well with Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma. The latter fell after getting a start and so did Dayalan Hemalatha but then came the big partnership between Smriti Mandhana and Kaur. The duo added 171 runs to the total and hit bowlers all over the park. Smriti Mandhana fell right after her century but Kaur took over the baton and along with Richa Ghosh added another 54 runs to get India over 320.

India Women have one foot over the series. What a knock from Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur! The two pillars of Indian cricket have entertained the Bengaluru crowd with some fine hitting. Smriti Mandhana scored her first run after almost 15 balls but she reached her ton on a run-a-ball pace. Harmanpreet Kaur on the other hand showed us why she is one of the best in this format.
Angling on middle, Kaur tucks it to square leg for a single. INDIA FINISH WITH 325 RUNS.

India Women showed great character and determination to take an early lead in this three-match ODI series. South Africa Women had the hosts in a troubling situation by dismissing their top order cheaply. However, a sensational century from Smriti Mandhana and a clinical performance from the spin arsenal turned the game around and took down the Proteas. India will expect a lot more from Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, and skipper Harmanpreet Kaur with the bat. They also have Richa Ghosh down the order, who can dismantle any bowling attack. Deepti Sharma and Pooja Vastrakar will play crucial roles with their all-round abilities. Asha Sobhana was excellent in the first game with a four-wicket haul, while Radha Yadav brings a wealth of experience. Renuka Singh has emerged as one of the best seamers the country has produced and has been very consistent at the international level. The Indian bowling attack looks formidable and will aim to keep the pressure on the South African batters. South Africa Women, on the other hand, will be disappointed as they were on top of the game but allowed the Indians to bat their way out and ultimately post a big score. Their batting needs to improve, especially against spin bowling. The likes of Laura Wolvaardt, Tazmin Brits, and Marizanne Kapp are experienced, and the team will be banking on some runs from them. Sune Luus looked in good touch and provides stability in the middle order as well. The Proteas' top order must find ways to counter the Indian spinners effectively. Ayabonga Khaka leads their pace attack and was impressive once again, along with Annerie Dercksen and Masabata Klaas. However, the spin department is a bit inexperienced, with Nonkululeko Mlaba and Nondumiso Shangase needing to do a lot more to exploit the conditions here. The Proteas will hope their bowlers can deliver early breakthroughs and contain the Indian batting lineup. As the series progresses, both teams have a lot at stake. The Proteas will be hoping to bounce back and level the series, while the Women in Blue will aim to seal the series with one game to spare. The battle between India's spin attack and South Africa's batting lineup promises to be an exciting contest. Let's see who comes out on top in this crucial encounter.
